dataset_family: Shanghai Memory Study (SMS; memory clinic cohort, Huashan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai; 41 MCI_C / 75 MCI_NC) for feature selection and internal CV, plus ADNI (25 MCI_C / 77 MCI_NC) as the second cohort. Neither overlaps the analysed samples of the current supporters (Sunshine Coast, Delaware, Bristol, 50-study synthesis, PREVENT-AD, NACC). P-581 uses AD-signature region definitions previously derived from ADNI data, but its analysed participants are NACC, so there is no shared sample.
method_family: Resting-state fMRI (static and dynamic ALFF, ICA inter-network FC and sliding-window dFC) compared with and combined with structural MRI (FreeSurfer: 68 cortical thicknesses plus 16 subcortical grey-matter volumes), SVM classifiers. rs-fMRI is the same method family as supporter P-518.
what_it_shows: For 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion, SVM models on rs-fMRI features and on structural features (thickness plus subcortical volumes) performed comparably: internal SMS AUC fMRI 0.90 vs sMRI 0.81, but ADNI AUC fMRI 0.76 vs sMRI 0.82. Adding fMRI to sMRI raised AUC in both cohorts (0.91 vs 0.81; 0.86 vs 0.82). There was no statistical test between AUCs. Converters had significantly smaller hippocampal and amygdala volumes at baseline, so volume was discriminative, not preserved.
why: Stated form (volume late/insufficient; function detects where volume is preserved): NO. At baseline, converters already showed reduced bilateral hippocampal and amygdala volume and cortical thinning (p.7). The structural model predicted conversion well (AUC 0.81 internal, 0.82 in ADNI), and in ADNI it beat the fMRI model (0.82 vs 0.76). Nothing in the paper shows prediction in a regime where volume is preserved or non-discriminative. Narrowed form (non-volumetric measures carry information beyond or comparable to volume): PARTLY. (1) Parity: the fMRI model performed 'similar with sMRI on external ADNI' (p.12). (2) Complementarity: sMRI+fMRI beat sMRI alone in both cohorts (Table 2, p.10). Limits: (a) The structural comparator is cortical thickness plus 16 subcortical volumes together, not hippocampal volume alone. (b) No significance test between AUCs; the fMRI advantage reversed externally. (c) Features were selected by group t-tests on the whole SMS cohort before 10-fold CV (p.6), so internal estimates are optimistic. (d) The ADNI arm is not a locked-model external validation: SVMs were rebuilt and cross-validated within ADNI on the SMS-selected features (p.6; 'the models constructed from SMS cohort were tuned when validated on ADNI cohort', p.12). Independence: SMS is a new dataset family, and ADNI is not used by any current supporter. rs-fMRI duplicates P-518's method family. No shared authors with supporters. Same university (Fudan) as candidate P-531, but a different hospital (Huashan vs Zhongshan), a different cohort (memory-clinic MCI vs Parkinson's), and no shared authors. Peer-reviewed (Human Brain Mapping 2024).

quotes.quote: The sMRI-based structural analysis showed significant reduction of cortical thickness involving temporal cortex (bilateral entorhinal, right middle, and inferior temporal), parietal lobe (bilateral inferior parietal and precuneus, left supramarginal, and right superior parietal) and right caudal middle frontal gyrus, and reduction of subcortical gray matter volume in medial temporal nuclei (bilateral hippocampus and amygdala) and left accumenbens, in MCI_C compared to MCI_NC at baseline (Figure 2).
The average cortical thickness of 68 cortical ROIs and gray matter volumes of 16 subcortical ROIs were chosen as candidate sMRI features for further feature selection.
followed by the sMRI model showing good performance with ACC/sensitivity/specificity above 73% and AUC of 0.81.
Based on these fMRI features, the fMRI model showed a good performance for MCI conversion prediction similar with sMRI on external ADNI dataset.
The multi-modality model, with AUC above 0.85 and average ACC/sensitivity/specificity around 80% in both cohorts, showed superiority to sMRI or fMRI solely
Finally, the features showing significant difference between MCI_C and MCI_NC patients were selected as the inputs of following prediction models.
SVM-based prediction model construction and evaluation, and the 10-fold cross-validation approach was also utilized in ADNI data, in consistency with SMS cohort.
Specifically, the models constructed from SMS cohort were tuned when validated on ADNI cohort, using same selected MRI predictors as inputs.
